pll2d2c1-d1e3516.summary: Notes that some authorities seem to imply angels were created before every creature.

pll2d2c1-d1e3519.summary: Cites Sir 1:4, 'wisdom was created first of all,' understood of angelic nature, often called life, wisdom, and light; not of the Wisdom that is God, which is not created, since the Son is begotten, not made.
claims: Created wisdom here means angelic nature.

pll2d2c1-d1e3534.summary: Cites Gen 1:1 and Ps 101:26 ('in the beginning you founded the earth') as saying God created heaven and earth first.

pll2d2c1-d1e3555.summary: States the apparent contradiction: if wisdom was created first, heaven and earth came after; if heaven and earth were created in the beginning, nothing came before; but Scripture cannot contradict itself, so the truth must be sought.

pll2d2c1-d1e3567.summary: Holds that spiritual and corporeal creation were made simultaneously ('he created all things together,' Sir 18:1), so angels were not prior in time to the matter of the four elements; wisdom was created first in dignity, not time. Augustine reads 'heaven and earth' as spiritual and corporeal creation, made in the beginning of time.
claims: Angels and corporeal matter were created together.
Angels are first in dignity, not time.

pl-l2d2c1.summary: Asks whether angels were created before all creatures, as 'wisdom was created first of all' (Sir 1:4), referring to angelic nature, not uncreated Wisdom, seems to imply. But Gen 1:1 says God created heaven and earth in the beginning. Lombard holds that spiritual and corporeal creation were made simultaneously ('he created all things together,' Sir 18:1), with angels prior in dignity, not time; with Augustine, 'heaven and earth' means spiritual and corporeal creation, made in the beginning of time.
claims: Sir 1:4 refers to angelic nature, not uncreated Wisdom.
Angels and corporeal matter were created simultaneously.
Angels are prior in dignity, not time.
'Heaven and earth' in Gen 1:1 can mean spiritual and corporeal creation.
